answers.bix-10-q1: In the multivariable ordinal logistic regression including BCG status, expected patient interaction, and patient volume, the odds ratio for higher COVID-19 severity associated with BCG vaccination (BCG vs Placebo) is 1.15 (approximately 1.149).
answers.bix-10-q2: In the ordered logit model adjusting for patients_seen_cat and TRTGRP_cat, the odds ratio for higher COVID-19 severity associated with expecting to interact with patients (Yes vs No) is 0.66 (approximately 0.657).
answers.bix-10-q3: In none of the patient volume groups (1–50, 51–100, >100 patients seen) is there a statistically significant (p<0.05) difference in COVID-19 severity between BCG and placebo groups; all p-values are >0.05.
answers.bix-10-q4: Among healthcare workers who expect to interact with patients, the chi-square test p-value for the association between BCG vaccination and COVID-19 severity is 0.173 (approximately 0.1732).
answers.bix-10-q5: For healthcare workers seeing over 100 patients, the p-value for the association between vaccination status and disease severity is 0.403 (approximately 0.4033).
answers.bix-10-q6: Among healthcare workers who see 1–50 patients, the chi-square test p-value for the association between BCG vaccination status and COVID-19 disease severity is 0.073 (approximately 0.0727).
answers.bix-10-q7: The odds ratio for higher COVID-19 severity among those expected to interact with patients is about 0.66; this corresponds to an approximate 34% reduction in odds (about 34.3%) compared with those not expecting to interact, controlling for BCG vaccination and number of patients seen.
